questions.stem: A swift car smoothly covers exactly 300 km in precisely 5 hours. What is its exact mathematical uniform speed?
questions.explanation: Speed = Distance / Time. Here, Distance = 300 km and Time = 5 hours. Speed = 300 / 5 = 60 km/hr.

questions.stem: A person securely crosses a 600 m long straight street in exactly 5 minutes. What is his precise speed in km per hour?
questions.explanation: Distance = 600 meters = 0.6 km. Time = 5 minutes = 5/60 hours = 1/12 hours. Speed = Distance / Time = 0.6 / (1/12) = 0.6 * 12 = 7.2 km/hr.

questions.stem: A man completes a long journey in exactly 10 hours. He securely travels the first half of the journey at the rate of 21 km/hr and the second half at exactly 24 km/hr. Find the total journey distance in km.
questions.explanation: Let the total distance be 2d km. So, the halves are d km each. Time for first half = d/21. Time for second half = d/24. Total time = d/21 + d/24 = 10. (8d + 7d) / 168 = 10 => 15d / 168 = 10 => 15d = 1680 => d = 112. Total journey = 2d = 2 * 112 = 224 km.

questions.stem: A boy safely goes to his school from his house at a steady speed of 3 km/hr and returns securely at a speed of 2 km/hr. If he smoothly takes a total of 5 hours in going and coming, the total distance between his house and school is:
questions.explanation: Let the one-way distance be d km. Time going = d/3. Time returning = d/2. Total time = d/3 + d/2 = 5. (2d + 3d)/6 = 5 => 5d/6 = 5 => 5d = 30 => d = 6 km.

questions.stem: Two energetic men independently start from opposite ends A and B of a linear track respectively and securely meet at point C. If the speed of the man from A is 5 km/hr and the speed of the man from B is 4 km/hr and the total track length is exactly 45 km, what is the precise distance between A and C?
questions.explanation: Since they move towards each other, their relative speed = 5 + 4 = 9 km/hr. Time taken to meet = Total distance / Relative speed = 45 / 9 = 5 hours. The man from A travels for 5 hours at 5 km/hr to reach point C. Distance AC = 5 * 5 = 25 km.

questions.stem: Excluding regular stoppages, the uniform speed of a bus is exactly 54 kmph and including those stoppages, it is precisely 45 kmph. For how many exact minutes does the bus typically stop per hour?
questions.explanation: Due to stoppages, the bus covers 9 km less per hour (54 - 45 = 9). The time it would take to cover this 9 km at its normal speed (54 kmph) is the time it spent stopped. Time = 9 / 54 hours = 1/6 hours. To convert to minutes: (1/6) * 60 = 10 minutes.

questions.stem: A quick thief is spotted closely by a vigilant policeman from a strict distance of 100 meters. When the policeman eagerly starts the chase, the thief also rapidly starts running. If the uniform speed of the thief be 8 km/hr and that of the policeman 10 km/hr, how far will the frantic thief have successfully run before he is firmly overtaken?
questions.explanation: Relative speed of policeman with respect to the thief = 10 - 8 = 2 km/hr = 2000 meters/hour = (2000 / 60) meters/minute = 100/3 m/min. Time taken to close the 100m gap = 100 / (100/3) = 3 minutes = 3/60 hours = 1/20 hours. Distance run by thief in 1/20 hours = Speed of thief * Time = 8 km/hr * (1/20) hr = 0.4 km = 400 meters.
